beliefs.practice: Create a single MongoClient (pymongo.MongoClient) at application startup and reuse it for all requests (singleton), configure maxPoolSize (e.g. 100) and close it on shutdown rather than creating a client per request.

Read the cluster connection string only from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) or from Azure Key Vault; never write the actual secret into logs, repo files, or example .env files (use .env.example with a placeholder).

Store production credentials in Azure Key Vault and have the service fetch them at startup (or use an identity-based secret retrieval flow) instead of baking plaintext credentials into environment/config files.

Create indexes on every field used in aggregation $match or $group predicates in production workloads (e.g. index {diagnosis:1}, {age_band:1}, {gender:1}, {region:1} and compound indexes for common multi-field filters such as {region:1, age_band:1}).

Materialized summaries stored in an aggregations_cache collection should include a UTC timestamp field (e.g. expires_at) and a TTL index created as db.aggregations_cache.create_index({"expires_at": 1}, expireAfterSeconds=0) to auto-expire cached summaries.

Design aggregation pipelines to filter and project early: move $match, then $project (to remove unused fields), then $sort/$group before heavy operations or $facet so the engine processes fewer docs (i.e. $match -> $project -> $group -> $facet when appropriate).

When materializing expensive aggregations, upsert documents with deterministic _id values (e.g. "summary:diagnosis_by_region:paramsHash") and include metadata fields (params, computed_at, duration_ms) so refresh jobs can atomically replace or update the cached summary with a single idempotent upsert.
Implement refresh/upsert operations as idempotent updates (use update_one(filter, {'$set': ...}, upsert=True)) so retries don’t create duplicate or inconsistent cache documents.

Wrap network/operation calls with exponential backoff + jitter and retry on transient errors (e.g. MongoNetworkError, socket timeouts, and 429/TooManyRequests from Cosmos), with a bounded max retry count.
For large or memory-heavy aggregation pipelines allow disk spill by enabling allowDiskUse=True in aggregate calls when supported (e.g. collection.aggregate(pipeline, allowDiskUse=True)).

Use explain() (or the documentdb MCP explain tool) on representative aggregation pipelines to confirm index usage and to detect COLLSCANs; if explain shows COLLSCAN add or adjust indexes or change pipeline order to avoid full scans.
When seeding synthetic datasets or performing bulk loads, use batched insert_many operations (e.g. batches of 500–2000 documents) rather than single inserts to reduce overhead and RU charge.

Monitor RU/s consumption and throttling (429 responses) and schedule heavy refreshes during off-peak times or temporarily increase throughput (or use autoscale) for materialization windows to avoid throttling and long-running queries.
Protect the cluster with network-level controls (firewall IP rules, virtual network/private endpoint) so only the backend service and trusted admin IPs can reach the Mongo endpoint.
Always use TLS/SSL when connecting (tls=true) and reject invalid certificates (do not set tlsAllowInvalidCertificates) so credentials are never sent over plaintext.

Emit telemetry for aggregation performance: record aggregation duration, RU charge (if available), document counts in/out, and cache hit/miss so refresh frequency and indexes can be tuned from observed metrics.
Limit aggregation result sizes returned to callers (summaries or pagination) and use projection to only return required fields to reduce network payload and client memory usage.
Prefer pre-aggregating high-cost summaries (materialized cache docs) for faceted dashboards and refresh them on a schedule or on-change rather than running the full aggregation on every HTTP request.
When building compound indexes, order index keys by query selectivity and sort usage (e.g. index {region:1, age_band:1} if queries filter by region then age_band; put the most selective field first).
For unit and integration tests, run against a separate test database name (e.g. sample_healthcare_16_test) and tear down or truncate collections between tests so tests never alter production data.

Guard against document-size limits when designing summaries: keep individual cached summary documents small (avoid embedding huge lists) and use paging or multiple documents if needed (MongoDB has a 16MB document limit).

If using vector search, store vectors in a dedicated field with consistent dimensionality, create the provider/engine-specific vector index with explicit dimension and metric, and test nearest-neighbour queries at scale; validate vector-index creation APIs for the Mongo API in your cluster before relying on it.
